Raphael Lemkin ( Polish : Rafał Lemkin ; 24 June 1900 – 28 August 1959) was a Polish Jewish lawyer who is known for coining the term " genocide " and for campaigning to establish the Genocide Convention , which legally defines the act. Following the German invasion of Poland in 1939, he fled the country and sought asylum in the United States , where he became an academic at Duke University and campaigned vigorously to raise international awareness of the atrocities that the Axis powers were committing across occupied Europe . [ 1 ] It was amidst this environment of World War II that Lemkin coined the term "genocide" to describe Nazi Germany's extermination policy . [ 2 ]
